utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I was informed that you'd like to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Very briefly, about one minute, to say the following: The situation is far from being simple, but we're going to deal with this now because as I understand, one part of the motion concerning the withdrawal is before the Bureau. I believe that we are now asked to formulate again this request before you and not before the Appeals Chamber because I believe that the President of the Trial Chamber I directly informed the Appeals Chamber that was about this. Our motion for withdrawal still holds. You remember that you asked us to support it with case law or with literature, so we have two possibilities: Either we can provide what we provided to the Appeals Chamber and you can give us your decision within a relatively short time; or you are going to ask us to integrate this into a new document that we would file before your Chamber with a copy of what we provided to the Appeals Chamber. I would like your clarification on this only on the motion itself for suspension.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... not quite clear to me. Do -- my understanding of the decision of the Appeals Chamber is that the matter is now pending before the Bureau rather than for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. As far as this is concerned, and as far as the request for suspension is concerned - I believe I said this, but this has to be dealt with quickly because we are near the end of our case - I believe that as far as the request for the suspension is concerned, it shouldn't be made before the Appeals Chamber but before your Chamber, and it is on this issue that I want your explanation and clarification. I don't know if I'm wrong. Would you be happy to be provided with what we gave to the Appeals Chamber, or would you like a new document? That's how we were instructed by the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you filed a copy just to inform the Trial Chamber from what you filed to the Appeals Chamber, and you're referring to, as far as I remember, the French Code of Criminal Procedure and some other systems. We'll deal with --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- this after the break. Perhaps we better look it and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There are some other matters as well that at some stage I'd seek to raise. I wonder if at the conclusion of this witness's testimony would be convenient to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are still -- let me just ask Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I ask for one second of your patience. Perhaps I meanwhile could ask you, Mr. Ierace, when do you expect that the still-pending translations of the suggested rebuttal evidence will be available?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can't say for certain, but it's quite possible that the outstanding translations will be available later on today. I'm told that the translation of Mr. Zecevic's material is expected later this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even if only parts would be ready, could you please provide them already to all portions that are available.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And perhaps I'm venturing too much into matters to raise later, but the maps, the further maps from Mr. From have been held up as a result of a technical problem in the OTP. But I can get into more detail about that later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, according to our calculations, the Defence took approximately their two hours. But I do understand that, I think, in some 10 to 15 minutes you could conclude this. Is that correct? Because we're now at 1 hour and 58 minutes. Then, Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would that be convenient to raise matters at the end of the witness's testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that would be fine, attend of the witness's -- so I would expect another 15 minutes for the Defence, so that would bring us to a quarter to 3.00. We'll have then one hour before the first break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Prosecution then -- so it will be just before, just after the next break -- the second break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that the registrar has a bunch of documents, including the one called -- numbered 1928 that should be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm glad that you were able to stay until today. And the Defence will have some more questions for you. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed. May I remind you. Perhaps you would have understand it also without saying, but you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, you will be shown a number of documents, in fact, Exhibit 1928. And I would like you to go through them very quickly, just to tell me whether you recognise them or not, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to these documents shortly. Before that, I'd like to ask you a question: In your career, did you have occasion to examine --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Exhibit 1928.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is a batch of various documents, apparently not one discrete document. As a matter of fact, I think the Defence calls reference to them as a bundle of documents. So perhaps we could ask what is meant by the witness saying "I recognise them." All of them or some of them or a particular set?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please make sure that out of the -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly, I would like to do it, but in the absence of the witness because I don't want her to be influenced and I don't want this to be counted in the time allowed to the Defence for questioning. So I would kindly ask that the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not fully understand you. You asked her to -- whether she recognised a bundle of documents. The only request would be whether you would be more specific so that we know what she does recognise and what he doesn't recognise, since it's a series of documents, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But they are interlinked, and this is what I'm interested in, this link between them. And I am happy to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... not you to answer but the witness to answer. It's -- we have lots of pages referring to what seems to be other documents, and I would like to -- just to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just asked one question of this witness, whether she recognises them, and she said yes. Now the Prosecution intervened and we have a problem. Maybe we could ask the witness to identify them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. Let me just ask you: When you say "I recognise this document," what do you recognise? What is the document? I mean, what does it consist of? Could you please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I recognise the document, although I don't know each individual case. I got this document to review and it contains reports with sources indicated for various cases of sniping, in terms of who submitted the information, et cetera. I can't say that I know each case in particular. I leafed through the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know certain cases, but not all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "I recognise this bundle as the bundle of documents concerning sniping incidents that has been handed out to me by the Defence."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, without focussing on this for the moment, did you have occasion to work on statistics which involve either household accidents or professional accidents or, for instance, traffic accidents?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, within the statistics of mortality we have violent deaths and violent deaths involve that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During your work on such accidents, what do we know about the place of accident? Is it mentioned? Is it known? Is it indicated? What do we know about that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the place of accident is mentioned, and it is one of the parameters for the statistics of mortality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you to focus on the first of these elements, namely the list of persons killed and injured for civilians in relation to sniping accidents. For instance, 00986277 and the following ones, and I would like to give me your first comment, in terms of statistics, that is, the number of pieces of information we have on the place of accident.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my first page is 792 -- my first page ends with 0277 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, we are talking about --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Here it is before me. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there should be several pages in this document. Do you see the number?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the number, but it's very illegible. Yes, I can see the number. Yes, this is better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us, madam, about this list? How many incidents are there where the place of accident is unknown? For instance, we have an accident with an injury or killing, presumably by sniping, and there is no indication of the place.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are cases of that kind. For instance, we have one dated 10th September 1992 and the incident is indicated without any indication of the place. Also the same date, involving the wounding of several persons, without indication of place. Furthermore, the 11th and the 12th September incidents, no indication of place of accident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll stop you, Doctor. You should comment only on the statistical aspect. Does this type of presentation of facts seem to you normal or abnormal based on what you know on the principles of compilation of statistical data for such reports?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't seem normal because official entities should certainly have information on specific incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you kindly go three pages further on the document to your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we are going to take, Mr. Usher, the page that is dated 24th of September. Do we have it on the screen? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we have the name in item 3, we have one person injured at Sedrenik, can you see that? And the name is Muhic.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, Vehbija Muhic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then date is -- the date is 27th September 1992. Madam, will you now take the list that you worked with the moment ago and will you please look at the date of 27th September 1992 and tell us what is written under the name of Muhic in the column titled "Place." And when you find this page --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Place unknown. Name, Vehbija Muhic. Born 1959. Evidence. Excerpt from --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you comment on this contradiction in terms?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's absurd. If you have evidence, if you have excerpts from documentation, people who are authorised to fill in this form, it may be the case of a deliberate omission, and I wouldn't like to go into the reasons why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the same batch that you have in front of you, you have a document in the Serbian language titled "U Slucaju Smrti," and the number is 0098784 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat the number for you, 00985724.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe the usher could help you to find it.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can show it to you so that you can see what it looks like. It's a certificate. As we are trying to find the document, we shall look at the second one, the second batch of documents under the number 1927, with the help of Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I do not find any translation of the documents you have presented at this very moment. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which one, Mr. President? Which one are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... the 27th of September, where it said that no place was known, whereas in the list it's called "Sedrenik" as far as I remember. But I might not have followed you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Mr. President, but the witness read the text in toto and it was translated for the transcript. The lady has written -- has read the sentence in question, and it is in the transcript because it was translated -- I do not think that we need any particular translation of it because it was interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To indicate the contradiction that we find there. But you want me to repeat it, Mr. President, this is -- this is the list produced in September 1992, and we find the same date that was just mentioned, that is, the date of -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I take it then the entry -- the first two lines starting with mjesto nepesnato [phoen], that was read, and then the name. Is that how I have to understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 27th of September, and that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's clear now to me. But I do take it then that the rest of the document we'll receive no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything was read out, everything was read out by the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'd like to go back to the other document, which is 1927, Madam, which you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And with the help of the usher, we shall also produce the necessary translations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I'd like you to concentrate on the first page, number 00 in the end and then page 5, which is the page 01 and therefore follows immediately after it, the previous one. And on that page 5 we have some figures which are of interest to us, and that is 73 to 77. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to read out to us, please - this is just one example - so will you please read to us what we have under 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could I be helped with trying to locate the page that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's the -- the pages are -- they were not in the correct order, but I rearranged them and I think it's the ERN number ending at 2901. That's the typed-out list. Have you found it? It's just behind the first page of the Exhibit 1927.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 75. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sadin Bogilovic, 14 September 1992, born in 1969, 10.15 hours armed conflict, several wounds, isolated injury, bullet both legs, and then there is the text in Latin. Do you want me to read that too? Vul sclopetarium reg. genus dex. I am not quite sure I am really familiar with Latin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That will be fine. Thank you. Indeed. Thank you, witness. Now, simply I'm looking at what is in the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do not have in the English transcript, Mr. President -- we don't have it there, but I believe I heard the witness and one of the booths speak about exchange of fire or fighting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I heard the French booth. It said "armed conflict," and that was not in the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, madam: This expression, "armed conflict," do we find it also in every one of the three cases between 73 and 79?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, would you now go back to the very first page with the number 900 -- I didn't say 905 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you for the B/C/S booth. I said 900.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to tell us if under -- in the column "sniper" we see the same name as the one that you mentioned between 73 and the following, that is, 78, 79, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we do, the second one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And there, madam, statistically speaking, do we find coherence here? What can you tell us about that? I'm talking about sniping and armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to be more precise, because I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Statically speaking, we have tables which attempt to establish the civilian victims of snipers and we have names which we see on page 900 and then -- and when we look at those same names on another list, we see that they were victims of an armed conflict. Do you think that we are dealing here with a problem of definition, or what can you tell us in this regard?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there is a problem concerning the definition here. Now, I could tell you what the official statistics does, unlike this. This is simply, does not agree with what the official statistics does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you explain it to us, but very quickly, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official statistics collects evidence about death, regardless of the manner in which those deaths occurred. And this evidence must be written out by a person who is called out, either a coroner or doctors in a hospital, if the person has been brought to the hospital. So there are diagnoses which the doctor must write accurately and he does that, the way that you do it in medicine. And those diagnoses, rather, or those notices of death, and without that there can be no statistics, and that is the statistics -- and that is the expert who goes into causes of that only and it is that which is then the basis for further work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you. We are discussing now a document. That document is not yet in evidence, is it, page 2901, or is it? Has this been produced before? I see you nodding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then before we discuss the document and what it says, that it's a list which tries to establish something, wouldn't it be wise to find out what the document is? I've got no idea, to be quite honest. So if you would please ask -- or perhaps I'll ask the witness. Could you please tell us, when you are commenting on the statistical meaning of this document -- well, let's say the numbers 73 and 75 onwards -- what is this document? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document represents excerpts from official records of the Institute for Emergency Aid in Sarajevo and then it lists the names and dates of incidents, persons, and a brief description of the time when an incident happened, where the person was injured, what were the circumstances of it possibly, and a short diagnosis in Latin. And I call it a diagnosis in Latin because I suppose -- I'm not really that fluent in Latin to know whether this is it, but this is in Latin, so I assume it was written by doctors.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document please be put on the ELMO, Your Honours, because the interpreters do not have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And there is also a stamp --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Yes. What does the stamp read? And may I first ask you, before you read the stamp, one question: On the other document, 1928, we saw an abbreviation ZHMP, which was translated as emergency health institute. Is that the same as this institute, and could you please read the stamp for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say. I suppose so. I think that that is the name of the institution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Can you read it? I have some difficulties in -- but I see "Sarajevo" both in Cyrillic and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is really barely legible, and I can't say. Perhaps if I had a magnifying glass or something. My eyes, I'm afraid, are not up to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether it has been produced during the war, after the war? You say these are excerpts from the -- could you tell us, has this been made during the war on the basis of what documents, or could you tell us something about -- if you don't know, it's no problem, but I'd like just to try to find out what is known about the document we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. are --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Yes. Then please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seem that is Judge Nieto-Navia has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please ask the witness to read again number 75, because the English interpretation was not complete. And I would like if she can read that very slowly so the interpreters can catch everything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should be happy to do that, Your Honour. But before that, Your Honour, could we ask the witness to read what we see at the bottom of the very first document, because that will tell us what is the list that follows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Only number 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you like this? Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Madam, will you read again number 75.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogilovic Sadin, 14th September 1992. 1969 at 10.15 armed conflict, a number of wounds, isolated injury, bullet, both legs. And then follows the Latin text. V or 5 point sclopetarium reg. genus dex et rega femoris sin [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, witness. I heard you tell us after 1969 and you said in your language "letter G." What does that mean? What does "G" stand for?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it means year, that is, the year of birth. Born 1969.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- Your Honour, Judge Nieto-Navia, are you satisfied with this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you asked the witness to read the first page, the last line as you intended to do, could you also ask the witness what is the relation between this first page and the other pages, because it seems to be quite a difference in --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Gladly. To my mind, there is not much to it. If we look at the ERN numbers, the first page has number 900 at the end and then the next one is 901 at the end, and therefore the Prosecution - since these are Prosecution's number - they received this document in this format and four pages are missing but perhaps it is a technical problem but it has no significance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please inquire whether there is significance or whether they received it in this order or whether they numbered it in this order, I do not know. The only thing I noticed is that this first page has a totally different type machine used. So I wonder what the relation is between these documents because we see some names are the same. So they certainly are in whatever relation with certain events, I take it, since they show dates that are -- seem to be the same, the 14th of September, they show names that are the same. But I do not know what is the exact relation between that first page showing to some extent the same data as on the other page, and I'd like you to ask the witness whether she knows what the relation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we read the last two lines of the document marked 900, and perhaps things will be clearer after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please read to us the three lines from the word "Dokaz," evidence?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Evidence, excerpt from the record from the protocol of the institute for emergency medical aid in Sarajevo to the name of wounded individuals."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you haven't read out to us the words Str 2.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Str 2 means page 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, and the pages that we saw and on which we have a list of names, do you think they're related, they're a follow-up on that first page?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because names from 73 to 79 can be identified with the names that are on page 1. Let me just check it once again. But I think that that is the case. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, witness. I'd now like us to proceed, and moving on this with document we shall stop on page number ERN 00985639. The page is in the -- halfway through the document. Shall I repeat it once again? 00985639. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the usher, the pages -- the page numbers are in the centre to the right, and it is January 1994. Mr. President, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it part --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because we have several of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Mr. Piletta-Zanin. They are numbered. Could you indicate what number you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is -- it belongs in the same list, and it is called "Wounded men." But I have six more copies, and I can give them directly to the usher. Perhaps it will be easier then. And we also have the necessary translations which we can also submit for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please accept the document from -- could we have a copy of the translation as well then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like the witness to look at number 3 to 9, numbers 3 to 9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have two more copies, for those who want them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to find the document in the original bundle, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, so that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it follows an Exhibit 638, and it is called "Snipers." But the time is January 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We finally were able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indicated the date, January 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... part of one of the exhibits that we have been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You -- it's approximately -- Mr. Stamp, it's approximately, I would say, just on face value, the twentieth page approximately, and it follows a page similar as to the front page but then with the 8th of January 1994 as the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like you to read to us what it says next to Nevan Andric.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nevan Andric, and then I think it says 0801, 1963 at 20.10 hours. Accidentally several wounds combined injury, bullet stomach, V transclopet abdominis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to ask you to look at 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9, the times of their woundings and the definition of their wounds.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5, it says at ten past 8.00, 20.10 hours, accidentally combined bullet pelvis. 6, at 20.10 hours, accidentally one wounded combined injury bullet stomach. 7, at 20.10, accidentally several wounds combined injury. Bullet hit stomach or abdomen. 8, 20.10 hours, accidentally several wounds, multiple injury, bullet R leg. 9, 20.10 hours, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. accidentally one wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Once again, can you comment from the statistical point of view only. We are talking here about the compilation of sniping incidents -- incidents. What can you tell us with regard to the time when these incidents happened? They all happened at ten past 8.00 and the definition "accident," could we hear your professional comment on that.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It said that. Yes, it says that those were all accidental.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But your comment?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my comment, well, it means that it happened by chance, something that -- that it was just a mishap, that -- I don't really understand what you want me to do. Do you want me to translate the word "accident"? Is that what you want me to say? Well, it happened as an accident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the usher, could we go back slightly and could we find document 0098229854. We are still talking about the compilation of sniping cases. And we have the translations, which we can produce. It is a document, a one-page document, usher, which begins --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us approximately how many pages we should move forward so --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fifth page. The fifth page, the fifth page from the beginning of the bundle. It's a document that begins with a handwritten note reading "EV" and then a number, 6802 -- sorry, 61012. Thank you. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you to read the penultimate paragraph, which begins with the words "according to the statement -- according to his statement."

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "According to the statement of his wife who was present on site, Sandrik Taljanovic, the bullet came from the direction of the field and hit the building, ricochetting and then hitting --" I can't see what follows very well -- "and then hitting Ismet." That's what it probably says. "Ismet," yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And we are going to pass to bullet 3360, which is approximately the beginning of the second third, and it's a document that looks like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm showing it to the usher. And the ERN number ends with 9115.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Might I just inquire. Is this the same bundle, 1927?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is. But to save time, usher, I suggest that you walk up to me and distribute this document to everyone because we have translations here. Thank you. We are going to hand out this to everyone, including the lady witness. Simply, because we have translations, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, in order to identify this document we are showing you now, in relation to the incident that you just read about, can you identify it?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can withdraw this document now. We are now going to focus on the list that I just indicated and that the usher had already found. Here it is. Madam, did you have occasion to study this list? Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But right now I can't see anything. Can I take it in my hands, because I can't say anything on the screen?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since we all have it and it's identified, I believe that yes, Madam, you can take it. Please. Right. Ma'am, have you studied, on the basis of this document, the figures for the injured and dead involving sniping compared to the table we saw in Ewa Tabeau's report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference between the figures in this document and the Tabeau report is that the Tabeau report gives a figure three times higher for people killed and four times higher for those injured. I can look it up if you allow me, and I'll tell you exactly what the difference is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we just clarify the answer and the question, because I think the question refers to people and in the reports there's a reference to civilians or soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Madam, when you say that the figures are higher, are you comparing comparable things? In other words, are you concentrating on civilians, on soldiers, or on both? Have you understood the question, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. Just give me one minute. Mrs. Tabeau gives a figure of -- let me see the table. Just a second. Here is the sum total. It gives a sum total, and it says 699 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Table 3. You can also use table 1. Tables 1 and 3 are identical. Mrs. Tabeau gives a total figure. She gives a sum total and says 699 killed and 3.111 injured from sniping. But when she breaks them down by types of death, she indicates both civilians and soldiers. For instance, you can see this on page 68, table 37 in the Tabeau report. It says "civilians, firearms, sniper rifle, civilian soldiers and status unknown." Altogether the figure indicated is 699. And on the very next page you see only civilians, 253; sniping fire, 253. So tables A37 and A38 in the Tabeau report. In the next line she gives us a figure of soldiers dead from sniping. The figure is 466. If we are talking about this ratio --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, having regard to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- perhaps counsel's question about the comparison between the figures for a document which refers to civilians, an unknown document which refers to civilians in comparison to the figures for Ms. Tabeau's civilians be compared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But before we do that, could I just ask you: You are now comparing, if I do understand you well, page 68 of the report of Ms. Tabeau with a list that was just on the ELMO which gives a, if I do understand you well, the list which -- let me just try and see. Could perhaps, would you please put the list -- yes, that one. Could it please zoom in. Yes. Could it please be moved a bit upwards, a bit upwards. Yes, please a bit more. Yes. Are you comparing this list with the Tabeau figures where you reach the conclusion that Tabeau gives figures far too high? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is just one small part, the tip of the iceberg. And I'm comparing this with the entire document that I had at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if you are comparing this document, which is now on the ELMO, with the table of page 68, do you know what time the table on page 68 covers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The table on the page 68 in Tabeau report. It refers to the period from 1992 to 1994, namely October 1992 -- sorry, September 1992 to the 10th of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you compare these lists in total, or did you limit yourself when you saw this last document to the time indicated by Ms. Tabeau? Did you start counting on the 10th of September, or was it the -- yes, the 10th of September or -- because I see a lot of earlier dates in this list. It starts, at least, with earlier dates. I see, apart from some number -- up till number 8 it bears no date at all and then number 9 starts with the 2nd of April; number 10, the 3rd of April; number 11, also in April. How did you count? Did you count them all, or did you count them starting from the 10th of September?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have a document dated 10th September 1992 to the 10th of August, 1994. This document is part of that document. And based on this document, which is dated as it is and which I got from the Defence, I made my calculation, only for that period which was under investigation in the Tabeau report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's the document which is on the ELMO at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, it's so illegible that I can't tell you on the basis of what I see on the screen whether it is that document or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in and go a bit more to the top so that you can see -- so please zoom in a bit more and then go to the top of that document. Is this the document you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the first page, I cannot conclude either way. But my document begins with the date of 10th of September, 1992, and it's also titled "Overview of identified civilians who were killed or wounded in the period from June -- or from 6," whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is the document the witness is now referring to, is that part of the bundle that has been given to the Chamber? And then would you please tell us where we can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the witness has in her hand, but it's not impossible that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not impossible that she has a summary that contains dates taken out of the document we just examined a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... recently. So that could you -- would you be willing to give it to us so that we can see what you are looking at and what you are comparing? If you'd give it to the usher, we'll have a look at it, I'll show it to the parties as well. Yes. If I'm not wrong, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think the witness had document 1928 in her hands. At least, it looks very similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The document that is being referred to my the witness is a document -- is the two preceding pages before the first page of 1928. So it's not among the bundle, but she might have been shown one of those or both of those pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that -- yes, it may be returned. It seems to be -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you get another 10 minutes to take care that the chaos that exists at this moment will be resolved and then we'll have a break. And you took one hour now, and you are -- it becomes rather incomprehensible if we do not know what the documents are about, if it's -- your questions are to some extent unclear, the answers are to some extent perhaps as a result also unclear. Would you please try to create some clarity until the break and then the Prosecution will have an opportunity to cross-examine the witness -- if there's any other --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Mr. President, I'm going to try to shed some light.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, witness, in other words simply speaking, what is your expert opinion regarding the Tabeau report and the figures you had occasion to study, whatever the documents that have been shown to you? Just tell us what you can to clarify the -- your position on the documents submitted by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... just too vague, and it comes back to the last objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it seems as if Mr. Piletta-Zanin tries to elicit some final conclusion. I do not -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I just said that vague questions give vague answers. But let's see whether the witness is able to answer a question. Let's see what the next question is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that Mrs. Tabeau based her report on completely inaccurate, inadequate, and biased sources, whereas she could have used much more reliable sources. I would not like to go into an explanation of why I believe the sources she used are unreliable, but as far as I can judge and from what was accessible to me, more reliable sources existed. These sources are not of such quality that they could be accepted without any dilemma, but at least they were verified by people who knew what they were doing. They were no amateurs. They were supported by certain institutions and procedures that could improve the quality of processing and sourcing of data. Of course in these sources we have only indications about the killed, no data about the injured. For instance, the source which is the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And as far as other sources are concerned, they are incomplete, they don't indicate the place of incident. And I have to underline that all that was accessible to me was the analysis made by Mrs. Tabeau and her associates and the overview of this document that I just commented on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion, is there a contradiction in terms in the Tabeau report? And if yes, then what is that contradiction? If the question not clear enough, I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many contradictions within that report. I will mention only one, but I can give you a broader comment if you like. Mrs. Tabeau first says that her sources were good and then when she tackles a certain democratic aspects [As interpreted], she comments that the sources are not so good. For instance, she has a number of sources such as the Bakija Funeral Parlour and the Muslims Against Genocide Association for certain items, but she always quotes one source without comparing them between them. There are other contradictions which I believe an expert cannot afford, should not allow herself. For instance, her total estimated numbers are based on unreliable arguments, and therefore later when she develops vital coefficients, she's unable to assess the structure of the population. There are many other contradictions in the report. I don't know how far you want me to go. It is my deep conviction that it is also contradictory to accept a job without any definitions and to make definitions yourself. I believe that before processing the census certain things that don't belong here should have been defined and excluded or she should have given explanations why she included them. She also included in her report, for instance, four to five thousand people who don't belong there according to the census. Furthermore, Tabeau does not give an explanation of what is an internal and what is an external definition of "soldier" and "civilian." She says also that the statistical area covered by the census is defined by the concept of local communes, saying at the same time that it all happened in 2001. We have to bear in mind the census was carried out in 1994. If you reconstructed the area where the census was done seven years earlier - and I don't want to comment on how qualified the people were who did it - and you didn't have proper data, you only had local experts and no help from statistics either, Tabeau only says that we bridged certain problems. I believe the bridging was done very badly because after all there is statistical data. In other words, this is all contradictory because the sources are not reliable and not good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question: We are going to examine in these documents - I think it will be very clear - there are many references to the place where the form is not filled. In other words, it says "place unknown." Technically speaking, according to your professional experience, this number of unknowns, which is rather high, does it have a direct impact on the conclusions of the Tabeau report? And if so, why?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, before that, the question was an impermissible comment about what is rather high or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was the comment? What was the comment that I made that was improper?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said that the number of unknowns are rather high. Whether it's high or not is -- that's the comment you made.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, very well. We have all seen these documents just a moment ago and we saw that there are many cases where it says "unknown, unknown, unknown, unknown." Everything is relative in this life. And if we look at the list that we submitted to you, it is striking how many place unknown indications there are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: According to what has been discussed before, the place is not filled in, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Is that ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether it's unknown --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... you could ask the same question exactly without such comment. You are suggesting something. Yes. So would you please try to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. But I thought I heard the witness saying that there were many such cases, and therefore I was asking her -- when I was asking her about household accidents, work accidents, traffic accidents, and she said, speaking of that, that there is a high figure for unknowns in that list. That's something that preceded from her answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put the question in such a way that -- you have given already so much comment until now. Let's just listen to what the witness wants to tell us about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, is there a high number of unknowns in this list, or is this number not high? And I'm talking now about list 6277.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a high number of unknowns, both in the list and in the results and tables given in the Tabeau report. I only counted the list, whereas I carefully studied the report and its tables. I will speak of something indicated in table 3 concerning the number of killed and injured. When she breaks down the incidents by municipalities, that is, the area that we should be looking at, Mrs. Tabeau says that Sarajevo is undefined, it is an unknown place, in other words. We see that there is over 10 per cent of unknown places in her report, including Sarajevo. And she indicates this after a very time-consuming correction that used such broad criteria, had no prescribed rules, statistical or otherwise, that she was free to decide for herself where one place belongs, in which municipality. So in such loose rules of the game you have supposed experts who allow themselves to decide where a certain place belongs, in which populated area, and the result is such a great number of undefined places, taking into account all of that, the quality is really poor. This is one of the indicators of really poor quality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here is my following question, madam: Regarding the definition of the sniper problem, the sniper issue, specifically speaking the presence of a certain X number of incidents of that kind, does that impact on the Tabeau report that there is an X number of unknowns?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so, because certain things are taken arbitrarily. Nothing is undefined -- in fact, I don't understand what you're asking me. Mrs. Tabeau took into account only the 1994 census and she didn't take into account this other list. I don't know if she knew that it existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to stop you here, madam. I was not talking about the census. I was only saying that in the list that we just saw a moment ago the victims, presumably killed by sniper, include an X number of unknowns. This X number of unknowns, is it of such nature that it could impact or influence the results, the conclusions of the report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but only because Mrs. Tabeau did not take it into account at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. It's time for a break. We'll continue at 4.15. We'll adjourn until then. And you'll then be examined by counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you asked for clarification in respect of paragraph 9 of the decision of the Appeals Chamber, which reads "That application should be made directly to that section of the Trial Chamber." So, therefore, the Trial Chamber expects the Defence to make an application so that the Prosecution then can respond, and we'll then further consider the matter. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But my question was, therefore: So it is you to whom I should submit that? Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Right. Just that we understand it really, and that is how we understood it. But my question was as follows: Would you -- if I make once again this application, will the Chamber accept that we had a great deal of things to do and that we have already made an appeal so it is -- so can we make further progress now in this regard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A new application should be filed just in respect -- you filed now an application that this section will be ordered to suspend. That's not -- that's not the basis on which we can proceed. So I take it that you'll then file a -- and it should not be long, but a brief request that this Chamber -- the section of the Chamber suspends the proceedings. And then Prosecution will have an opportunity to answer to that. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, madam.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you speak or read English?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not particularly well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the curriculum vitae which you attached to your statement, you indicated that you completed the Faculty of Philosophy in 1975. Did you complete it with a degree or did you not?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had a degree of graduate ethnologist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And ten years later you did your -- well, you completed your masters degree. And in 1999, you did a Ph.D. thesis and to your credit became chief of the department three years after you had defended your Ph.D. thesis.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you published any work outside of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that one or two of my papers were translated outside. Do you want me to answer that three years later I became the head of the department? Does that have any significance or not? I mean, I didn't understand whether it was a question or just a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in the period of time between your degrees, you have worked consistently in the area of population census methodology; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My first job was with the statistics institute. I worked 18 years there. And part of that, I was the head of the department for population statistics. I participated in three censuses. In 1971 I regulated that in Serbia. I was a member of all the expert groups for the former Yugoslavia, for the census of '91. Then I was a consultant in 2002 for Serbia. And in 1981 I was a member of the expert team for methodology, that is, the organisation that dealt with the methodology of conducting the population census.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it correct that all your training and scholarship during your career has had to do with research into the methodology of population censuses and the results of these censuses?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not the only thing that I did. I did many other things. But I am highly conversant with the census methodology, especially at the time when I worked at the statistics institute, because that was my job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, is it correct that your field of expertise is in the area of population censuses?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is much broader than that. It is the census statistics, or rather, population statistics and demography. I teach demography, and my Ph.D. is also in demography. But all this, of course, is closely related to the population statistics because the -- because the statistical methods -- population statistical methods are very important in demographic studies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Demography, then, is a field within the -- which there might be different areas of expertise. For example, you have persons with the expertise in census demography and you might have persons with expertise in other areas of demography. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. But there is no such thing as census demography. There is population statistics, which is used in demography.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, are you aware of a field of expertise within demography involved in deriving statistics in situations of complex humanitarian emergencies?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I am. But you have to be more specific. When you say "are you aware," if somebody is aware of the population statistics and demography and if it has to do primarily with statistical data, because demography is a multi-disciplinary science, it encompasses many things, and the population statistics is something else. It is a method -- it is a statistical method which you apply in demography.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you -- you said you're aware of the field of expertise involving the methodology used in complex humanitarian emergencies. What are the methods used in demography as applied to complex humanitarian emergencies?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please define "complex humanitarian emergency situation."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I do that with the help of a document. If the usher could assist me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an extract from a presentation on the roundtable on the demography of forced migration, mortality and population. Are you aware of that roundtable?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to tell me where, because I can't read it here. I can't see where and when was it held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- are you aware that the roundtable is an ongoing project by demographers who specialise in the areas of investigating complex issue humanitarian emergencies?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't tell me where it was held and when, and where is that roundtable? Like, this, I can't recognise anything. I am currently involved in a project in Serbia addressing the same subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it's not this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm indicating and what I'm asking, ma'am, is whether or not you're aware that the roundtable is the collection -- an ongoing collection of a body of work from specialists involved in a particular area of demography, referred to as statistics for complex humanitarian emergencies? Are you aware of that; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still don't know who organised -- who is its organiser, where it happens. I am looking at this page, and I don't know what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could come back, Ms. Radovanovic, to one of the earlier questions. The question was whether you were aware of -- I think there was a reference to complex humanitarian emergency, and then you said what do you mean by that? And then Mr. Stamp said, I'll tell you but I'll use a document for that. And this document, as I read it, says, "The term complex humanitarian emergency is widely used to describe a particular type of disaster, a situation in which a large civilian population is affected by a combination of civil or international war or a gross attempt to restructure the state or society, such as genocide, leading to a large-scale population displacement with accompanying deterioration of living conditions, such as food, potable water, shelter, and sanitation, creating the potential for a significant increase in mortality, typically during some limited period of time but sometimes lasting much longer." The question we started with was whether you are aware of any specialism which specifically deals with this subject in demography.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, interpreter's comment: The witness does not seem to be aware that there's a translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is -- if you would like to reread it, the next pages give a translation of what I just read to you, that is, the first paragraph of the last page of this document. So the answer was that you heard of it, and I take it that you have now had an opportunity to read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About this type of research, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I may read the last sentence of that first paragraph: "Examples of complex humanitarian emergencies in even more recent years include wars, ethnic cleansing, forced migration, and genocide occurring in place as varied as Somalia, Bosnia, Rwanda, Kosovo, Sierra Leone, and East Timor." Would you consider the circumstances that obtained between 1992 and 1994 in Sarajevo to be a situation of complex humanitarian emergency?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could put it that way, even though I am not fully familiar with all that. But looking at it as a whole, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like Mr. Stamp to make his question more specific. What does he mean by "Sarajevo"? Does he include Nedzarici? Does he include Ilijas? And so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was clear enough. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp. And the witness had no difficulties in understanding it, and we're just talking at this moment about a situation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, madam, you yourself said that you know not of any situation where a census was taken during any war. Do you know -- or let me rephrase that. Is one of the purposes of a population census to measure human casualties even in normal times, or is the measurement of human casualties, for example, road traffic accidents, et cetera, even in normal times the result of the ongoing registration by official sources of vital events, births, deaths, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of a population census may also be to include human casualties, and so on and so forth. It depends on establishing the objectives of the population, depending on the interest of the society conducting the population census. So whether the census in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 2003 or 5 or 7 will have as one of its objectives the registration of the victims of casualties, that will be the decision of Bosnia-Herzegovina, if they consider it to be of their interest. A census is an all-embracing activity, the population census, so that such an objective may be included. So far in the territory of the former Yugoslavia I am not aware that regular population censuses, that is, household censuses, had such an objective included. I am not aware. In 1964, maybe 1965 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you'd agree with me that generally speaking, as far as Yugoslavia is concerned, censuses are really -- the objective of censuses is to measure the socioeconomic conditions of the living and the measurement of deaths and casualties is a result of the ongoing registration of vital events by official channels?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand your question, you said that the objectives of the Yugoslav censuses were not to also take a record of all the victims. Well, it depends. There was a census of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia which pursued that objective. But as of World War II onward, no, that was not one of the objectives. They simply had the statistics -- the statistics regarding deaths, regardless of what kind of death, that is done through vital statistics, which are independent of population censuses. As for --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So having regard to these two agreed points, that you would not really have a census in circumstances of a war of a complex humanitarian emergency, and you'd not really -- or generally speaking use a census to measure things like deaths or casualties, on what basis do you call the point of Ewa Tabeau, et al. a census and you'd base your examination and on an analysis of it from the point of view of it being a census?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is Ms. Tabeau who does that. In her analysis, at least in the Serbian translation, she calls it the household census 1994 conducted in Sarajevo from so and so and then she says 1st of January, so on and so forth. I did not call it a Serb population census. It wasn't mine. I just took over that from the report that I had before me. The word "census" is used in the expert opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you find one example of that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here. Of course I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report in the Serbian translation - and I won't be able to quote the page number in English - here, for instance, table 1 says, "Overview of summarised statistical data from the census of households in Sarajevo 1994." Then chapter 1 goes as follows -- sorry, chapter 3: "Census of households, that is, the household survey on the free territory of Sarajevo in 1994 (HSS 1994)." And then, speaking of tables I can go one by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the word --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are called from the PDS census.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the word you see there for a census?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where here? The entire chapter is titled --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is saying in Serbian "census of households, census of households in the free territory of the city of Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then in -- then below, PDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What chapter?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's chapter 3. But if we start from the beginning, if you want me to proceed that way -- chapter 1, we can start from the summary, if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, could we try to get a clarification perhaps from the interpreters on the word used in the B/C/S and in English. I don't know whether there's any difference of view, because the -- do we know -- I haven't got in front of me the B/C/S version of Ewa Tabeau's report. Could you please when you say the word "census" as it is translated to us, what is it in B/C/S? What is it in your own language? Could you pronounce it in your own language so that we receive the word, not translated, through the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Popis" in the Serbian language is the same as "census" in English or in Latin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask the interpreters, apart from the explanation given by the witness, how would you translate the word "popis" as far as I understand it to be.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Census."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Census." Would the word census be something different from the word we find in English, which is survey, the household survey? How would you translate in this context the word "survey" into B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what "survey" means. I know what census means because of the Roman census.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. But I'm now asking the interpreters to tell us how they would translate the word "survey" and specifically whether they would translate it or -- using the word "popis"? And I see that some work is done.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is from the B/C/S booth. The word that I would use for "survey" in backwards would be either "pregled" or "istrazivanje", which is similar as "research" but "pregled" would be a better choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I hear from our interpreters that they would choose the word "pregled" to translate the English word which says "survey." It seems that at least there is a linguistic problem. I don't know whether it's the only problem or whether there are more problems, but perhaps we should keep this in mind when we continue. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the heading of section 3, what word do you see there, "popis" or "pregled"?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every chapter it says "popis". Not in a single chapter, not in a single part of this text is the Serbian word "pregled" used. But if you would allow me, I would like to comment on the word "pregled," or survey, in order to disagree with it. In view of the volume that is in question here, in view of the way in which everything is explained here -- of course I'm not an expert in the Serbian language, I cannot claim with absolute certainty that the word "pregled" is closer to "survey" than the word "popis" or "census." But in view of the mass scale involved, I believe that "census" is closer to the actual notion. "Survey" is something that implies a much shorter period or excerpts taken. I could argue with it. At least, I believe it is arguable. But if you consider the word "survey" in the translation of "pregled" to be more adequate, I am prepared to agree with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see section 2. Could you have a look at section 2 of the report of Tabeau et al.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you have a look at the second paragraph of that section.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see in the second sentence of that paragraph the words "our major source," or do you see the second sentence beginning with "our major source, the household survey on the free territory of Sarajevo"?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second paragraph begins in my text as follows: "Our principal objectives are to provide reliable statistics on population losses," and so on and so forth, and to compare them with the pre-war mortality ratios. I can't see what you are --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you just read on --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- mentioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read on, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here. "All this can be done as the sources used -- as the sources used for this report are extensive. Our major source, the household survey --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's comment: The word in Serbian again is "census".

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
