utterances.text: -- on the free territory of Sarajevo in 1994 is a questionnaire, is a census-like population survey in the area within front lines in Sarajevo at mid-1994. Thus, it was expected to cover the entire population living in this area at the time the survey --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Again, the word used is "census"?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was conducted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So madam, that section that deals with the sources of the reports and that part that you read in particular would have put you on guard that the report of Ewa Tabeau was not strict a censor -- a census but was a census-like survey. And as you are well aware, you would not have a census during a war.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg to differ, for the simple reason that even censuses are conducted through the use of questionnaires. In other words, the method used in the majority of countries, including Yugoslavia, the former Yugoslavia, is the questionnaire. You take a questionnaire and you go on to carry a census. So maybe Ewa Tabeau thought she was making a survey, but you seem to be saying that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw the word "like population survey," what did you understand those words to mean?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw the word "census-like survey." It says "census" everywhere. I never came across the words "census-like" and all the questionnaires were made up in that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought you just read from the section in the report which deals with the survey that it describes a household survey of the free territory of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, could we please ask the witness to read again slowly the sentence starting with "our major source, the household survey on the free --" could you please read that sentence slowly. And may I ask the specific attention of the interpreters for the second part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Our major source, the census of households in the free territories of the city of Sarajevo in 1994 was -- is a census-like population poll in the area within front lines in Sarajevo in mid-1994. Therefore, it was expected that it would cover the entire population living in this area at the time the census was conducted."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that you never saw the word "census-like population survey." Could we please ask the interpreters what in the original language -- because there might be a translation problem again. You translated it as a "census-like population survey." What does it say in the original B/C/S wording just read so that we can identify if there's a linguistic problem? Could I ask the booth to -- especially the B/C/S booth to tell us what the original wordings were.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the original -- in the original, there are three words, Nalik Na Popis, which means "census-like."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In respect to the body of world in the field of demography concerned with complex humanitarian emergencies, what sources have been suggested as appropriate for measurement and assessment of casualties and democratic -- I beg your pardon, demographic factors?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of network sampling? Could you explain that to us, and snowball sampling.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense? I know, for instance, about the network sampling of populated areas in Serbia. Are you interested in that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in the application of those two types of sampling to demographics in complex humanitarian emergencies. Are you aware of the use of that type of work in that situation.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about that, but that has nothing to do with this analysis, with this report that was given to me to examine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wouldn't you say it's -- well, what is network sampling? And wouldn't you say that this survey was an example of network sampling with some element of snowball sampling? Or do you know? Were those terms designated in the field of the demographics of complex humanitarian emergencies?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that this report is an example of such network sampling for the simple reason that it was conceived in a completely different way. And then on we could argue about the sample taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And whether it is adequate to the method --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area of complex humanitarian emergencies, what is network sampling?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that again depends on who is doing what, what type -- what team of experts is going where with what mission, whether it is using a sample provided it or making its own sample. So there is no generally accepted prescribed way to proceed. That is decided ad hoc from situation to situation, from expert to expert, with the desire to do the best job possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would not be prepared to give us a definition of network sampling in so far as it is applied in complex humanitarian emergencies.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I could not give you a definition, nor do I believe that there is a universal definition so that everyone dealing with demographics or population statistics know it. It is just one of the ways to go about a certain task in the area of demography or statistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, and with the assistance of the usher, could the witness be shown a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be P3775.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's a document entitled "Demographic assessment techniques in complex humanitarian emergencies." And it is the summary of work presented by experts in that field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at page 2 - and there's a translation of that at the back. I beg your pardon, page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Radovanovic, may I ask you not to make any markings on the copies you receive unless specifically asked to mark it. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is indicated that at least three major organisations have published guidelines on how to conduct initial demographic assessments, Medecins sans Frontieres, the United Nations High Commission for Refugees, and the Sphere Project. Each of these sets of guidelines vary slightly but their purpose is the same, to help field workers obtain a base-line estimate of the total population and its vital characteristics." Are you okay with the guidelines and methodologies for estimating the populations in areas subject to complex humanitarian emergencies?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the methodology of population assessment not in humanitarian organisations though. But that's precisely what I'm talking about. This is a convention on how to proceed about certain tasks, so that experts in the field could adhere to it, which doesn't mean that experts who adhere to it should be using bad sources. So I have nothing to do -- I have nothing against the technique. It is a matter of convention. We say "this is the situation as it is and this is how we'll do the job," but an expert has to be able to decide whether the information used is good and reliable or it is bad and provides a completely distorted picture of what we are trying to ascertain. So I have absolutely nothing against this as a technique to be used in complex humanitarian emergencies. What is important is that the experts make sure that this assessment is based on correct data, data which does not give a distorted picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look, if you will, at some of the techniques referred to by the experts in the demography of complex humanitarian emergencies. And I'd like to read a part from page 11. "Human rights abuses, violations of international standards of human rights, such as kidnapping, rape, torture, and genocide, are traditionally documented through testimonies and clinical or forensic evidence. Now, these methods are being used in combination epidemiological and demographic models. Cluster sampling is not appropriate for measuring mortality in cases of human rights abuses because they are not random event. Some non-probability sampling techniques that might work in these situations include network sampling, in which more than one individual can report on another individual in the survey, multiplicity, or snowball sampling, which uses a process of chain referral by members of the population of interest, an adaptive sampling which is a technique often used for studying disease patterns among wildlife in which if a diseased animal is discovered, then additional animals are sampled in the same area." Would you agree with me that the experts recommend network sampling which is -- in which more than one individual can report on the victim -- on another individual who is a victim?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. I understand what you're saying. Experts do recommend that it may be so. But experts do not recommend that such a sample can be transposed onto the entire population. If you have a sample, it has to be of such a quality that it gives a picture of the overall phenomenon. In this report, we should be dealing with, we are dealing with a sample that does not provide a good picture, a faithful picture of the overall phenomenon and the method used varies from report to report. Of course, even if one person reported a victim, it should be enough, but it all depends on where, at which level, with what objective. This is a very idiosyncratic, very specific analysis that deals with people who are killed or wounded. It generally applies to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- a massive population that has not even been nearly defined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can agree that it is a very specific area of expertise, but would you agree with me that persons experienced and accomplished in this area, this field of demographics, can use a variety of sources, even sources from so-called perpetrators, and once they are aware of the limitations of the sources they can come to conclusions in respect to the rates of casualties during a complex humanitarian emergency?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that experts can do that. But first they have to assess to what degree, how much sense it makes. I have to elaborate on this. If you want me to use a sample, for instance, in this courtroom based on this recommendation by your experts, I can say that people over the age of 60 are tried, people are tried if they come from Bosnia and Herzegovina, people are tried if they are generals, people are tried if they are graduates of military schools. So if you use this recommendation, you are still not guaranteed to get a faithful picture. An expert is duty-bound to make an assessment and say I'll accept this method or I will not accept this method. If you are dealing with statistical analysis and demographics --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm enquiring, madam, is your level of knowledge and expertise in a particular field of demography. So we just want to discuss certain areas of methodology. And if you don't know about something, you can say so.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. I just don't understand why you are asking me this, because this analysis, this report is not grounded in what you are talking about. In fact, more precisely, the way it is written, the way these phenomena are treated, doesn't seem to be indicative of this. Maybe you can use one statement, maybe one sample is used. I believe an expert has to be very cautious, has to make an assessment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cannot allow himself to make the conclusions as are given in this report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you then repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me - and I will read the last sentence of the -- of page 12 of this document before I ask --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please do that slowly, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Depending on the ultimate use of the data, precision and reliability may be more or less important. For example, data precision is generally very important in legal cases, such as human rights tribunals." Madam, is it because of your lack of familiarity with this area of demographics why you frequently criticise the report of Tabeau et al. as using redundant statistics?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am not sure that -- no, you do not know whether I know that or not. I am telling you they know what this is about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm not criticising Mrs. Ewa Tabeau. What I am criticising is sources and the way in which it was done. It has nothing to do with Mrs. Tabeau, because she just happens to head that team and I am involved in this kind of work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've answered. Would you agree with me that in using the methodologies of the demographics of complex humanitarian emergencies for human rights tribunals or truth commissions the requirement would be to conduct the study and the research in such a way as to present the minimum numbers possible as Tabeau et al. have indicated they did?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with you. I think you are confusing two things. One thing are demographic methods, the methodology used in demographics, and I can talk about that. The other thing are sources of data that you use so that by applying those methods and with the help of the statistical method you could arrive at explanation of certain things. In other words, I do not agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I think it would certainly assist the Chamber if we do not stay too much on the abstract theoretical level. I mean, if you asked the witness whether she considers herself an expert and that's part of your questions, you could not easily expect her to say no, I'm not an expert at all. And that's more or less the line of questioning at this moment, and I don't think -- let's try to get out of the two abstract levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's -- madam, you heard what the President said. Let's get to something a little more practical. In your report at page 2 of the English version you said that "The estimation of human casualties with application of the method for determination of an unknown volume of animal population, one can produce the greatest possible confusion in the perception of and conclusion in the significance of relevant statistical indicators." And further on at page 50, you said, "The applied method of occupation, that is a capture-recapture technique was not sufficiently explained and we do not know that in the demographic research it had ever been applied before." You do not know that in demographic research capture-recapture -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I'm sorry but I don't have page 50 in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can I just check.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, Your Honour. It's the last paragraph of page 43.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I was just referring you to a part of your report in which you said that, to quote, "We were not aware of it being used in demographic research." Are you aware that in respect to the demographic analysis for human rights purposes of complex humanitarian emergencies the capture-recapture methodology has been used in a variety of countries, Vietnam, Guatemala, even in Kosovo, as it has been used by Tabeau et al.? Are you aware that it has been used or is your statement in your report that you are not aware of it correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I've heard about the method -- or rather, that Mrs. Tabeau did not proceed in a manner which is normally used in the scientific world. She does mention certain methods and says that they are in use, but she doesn't say where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... You wrote in your report that you do not know of the methodology of capture-recapture being used in demographic research. I'm asking you if you still maintain that you do not know of it being used in demographic research. Is what you wrote in your report still your state of mind? That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to see what I wrote in my report. If you will excuse me. Can you tell where is that. What are you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... of your report, first sentence.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the following: "If we agree that one can apply -- I mean, this method, that one can apply this method in a specific demographic study, then we cannot agree with the quality of the sample used because this method requires two independent and impartial samples and requires that these samples be large. Now, we can discuss what is a large and what is a small sample. So I agree, I didn't say I didn't know. I merely said that the manner in which it was done to my mind was not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just answer me one thing: Did you say in the first sentence of the last paragraph of your report "We do not know that in the demographic research it had ever been applied before"? Did you indicate that? The first sentence of the last paragraph. It's a simple yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The applied method of capture was not sufficiently clearly explained and we do not know that in the demographic research it has ever been applied before. That is what I said. But I agreed with the method as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, madam --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And sorry, the lady was duty-bound to comply with the scientific and other literature so that I could educate myself and know what she's talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please refrain from such comments unasked for. The only question to you at this moment was whether you'd stick to your observation that you do not know that in the demographic research this method had ever been applied before. That was the question. And we never asked Mrs. Tabeau to comment on the way -- how you performed it. If there are any specific observations you'd like to make, you will get an opportunity to do so at the end. But please first answer to the questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I take it from your answer, madam, that you needed to be educated in how the capture-recapture method is applied to demographic research in complex humanitarian situations. The document I showed you last, if I may just read a part of page 12. "Patrick Ball of the American Association for the Advancement of Science presented some of his work on measuring human rights abuses in a variety of settings. One effective method is called capture-recapture, in which one member of the sample is selected, "returned" to the population, and if the same person is selected again, she or he is 'tagged.' Originally developed for use in counting populations of animals or fish, for human rights research the method uses administrative data that were kept by the perpetrators. Because more than one witness may report a killing, some killings may go unreported, and there are often several sources of testimonies, multiple lists of killings are often available and must be used to estimate the actual number of murders. According to the theory behind the capture-recapture method, the level of overlap, or the number of killings reported by two independent lists, makes it possible for investigators to estimate the number of killings that occurred in the total population including those killings that were not recorded in either list. The method was used in Guatemala following the civil war in that country (1954-1996)." And it indicates what the calculation was. But more importantly, at the beginning of the next paragraph - and I'm referring you now to the use of the capture-recapture method which has been used before as testimony in court - "Ball and his colleagues also conducted a study during the recent war in Kosevo (1999) using lists from three different organisations."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Ball and his colleagues also conducted a study during the recent war in Kosovo using lists from three different organisations." Are you aware of that study?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were aware of the capture-recapture method being applied to the field of demographics in complex humanitarian situations. You were aware of that, were you?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about the method. I am not aware that it was applied in the Balkans. To demographic complex emergencies, I didn't know that that was the common practice. Yes, I know about the method. I know what it is. But I do not think it is applicable. The rules of humanitarian organisations, so on and so forth, I fully respect them, I do not begrudge Mrs. Tabeau the use of that method. I am not discarding it. I accept the method. That I didn't hear that it was a part of some Balkan or Bosnian studies, that is another matter. But what I am saying, that such a method requires two independent sources, a particular sample, a specific size of the sample, and that is what we can discuss. And I am saying that a sample was not a representative one. But I absolutely do not hold it against Mrs. Tabeau for using that method, especially since she uses this for population estimates. But the problem is that the basis, that the starting point is wrong. That is that the sources we are using to arrive at something are not good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... You said you have heard about the method and I am not aware that it was applied in the Balkans. Isn't a particular area of your work as a demographer a study of ethnic differences in Kosovo and the statistics in respect of the population in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Kosovo, the population of Kosovo and Metohija was the subject of my doctoral thesis, but I used official verified sources of information such as population censuses. I also a conducted polls, certain questionnaires. I did not use this method. I had no need to use it because there are exact data. I was making no guesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look quickly, if you will, at a third document. This is research done in the capture-recapture methodology in respect of political killings in Kosovo. Are you aware that the research has been used in human rights cases, or at least one human rights case, madam?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll accept what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a question. Are you aware? And the answer is either yes or no. Either you know or you do not.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you tell me whether the method was used as assessment, I haven't heard of that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Madam, since you don't know about it, then I'll take you through it. But I'd just like you to look at the bibliography at the back of this paper that you have been presented with. Just browse through it briefly and tell me if you'd agree with me that the capture-recapture method is a standard methodology used by specialists, demographic specialists in the field of complex humanitarian emergencies, by epidemiologists and victimologists. Have a look another the document, please, the bibliography of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please, usher, could you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are not looking at it, ma'am. Could you please look.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will disagree with you when you say that it is a standard method. I am not saying that it cannot be used. I'll find you a number of demographers who do not use it. Once again, I have nothing against the method. It is used for estimates. And I'm not disputing -- I'm not questioning the method. I'm not even questioning the estimates which were arrived at on the basis of that method. What I am questioning are the sources used to arrive at a sample. The methods are fine, the estimates are fine, but the sample is wrong. And if the sample is wrong, then your estimates cannot be right either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Radovanovic, may I ask your attention for the following: There seems to develop itself a debate where -- which started where questions were put to you on a specific line of your report where you say that you are not aware of a certain method to be used in demographic research. Mr. Stamp is putting to you some material which in his view would demonstrate that there is literature that indicates that such a method was used in demographic research, and slowly it seems that you're shifting to another subject, which is whether this system should have been used in this research done by Ewa Tabeau. Let's try to clearly separate the issues at stake. So, for example, if you say I can show you a lot of researchers who do not use the method, if one says that it's frequently used, then of course there is others who do not use it. But it was not the question whether all researchers used it, but we started at -- that you were not aware of the use of the method and we slowly developed to the question whether all used them and then we moved to another item, that is, whether it was properly used under the circumstances. I'd like to invite you to listen carefully to the questions and try, together with Mr. Stamp, not to mix up different issues. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, madam, I would like to ask -- let me withdraw that comment. You, madam, at various passages in your report to make some specific criticisms of a number -- of numbers, do you understand that for the purpose of -- well, for a variety of purposes, one being transparency, when a report is done in respect to casualties that occurred during a complex humanitarian emergency, the report includes a variety of characteristics of a sample or samples that were used for the report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that. But here we are dealing with samples which need to be in the report and those which need not be in the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We want to move through as quickly as possible. You say that the report of Tabeau et al. dealt with undefined parts of Sarajevo. Is it not clear right through the report that it is dealing with a part of Sarajevo within the confrontation line, sometimes called the free territory that was under the control of the government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Isn't that clear to you from reading the report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because this report does not address a space. It says "within Sarajevo," and then it says "smaller parts of six municipalities." Then it says "the free territory." And when I read the report, I do not know where are the military, where are the political boundaries. I know that this area is not defined in a way in which you could poll the population without incurring a major risk, be it for a census or for a large sample or whatever. So statistically speaking, that space has not been defined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it might not have been confined in the context of official census statistics, but within the context of a complex humanitarian emergency can you understand or do you understand that the report purported to deal with the area within the confrontation lines of Sarajevo? Can you understand that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can understand it, but I disagree. Within the certain area, the report said that it statistically it takes over 89 local communities. So in one case we have statistical -- statistical method used and in another no. When it says over 89 local communities, that is not a statistical value. But your expert said we statistically defined it so and so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to have a look at some of the figures that you used or that you specifically criticised. You said at page 10 of your report - and that's the English version - perhaps I could assist you in finding where it is in the Serbian text. That is at the end of a long paragraph which is the second paragraph of section 2.1.1. "As data from the same source and from the same space that is, PDS 1994 several different magnitudes are given --"

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not getting the interpretation. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any problem, Ms. Pilipovic, with the interpretation at this very moment? Yes. Is there any --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic's microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your microphone is still --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am getting the interpretation but not the general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are not receiving the translation. Could we please check that there are --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's all right, Your Honour. I didn't get only the end of Mr. Stamp read out. All the rest I had and I could follow. It was only the end of Mr. Stamp's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Question, yes. Could you please repeat the question so that both General Galic and of course the witness could hear your question, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end of the second paragraph of section 2.1.1 of your report, you said, "Furthermore, a confusion of terminology, territory, and time is being used for the purpose of imposing false images of the events which are being explained in the report. Just as data from the same source and for the same space, that is, PDS 1994, several different magnitudes are given. For example, persons killed inside the front lines in Sarajevo can amount to 3.798, 3.225, 3.689, but also to 7.879 and 6.055 or 2.963." And you quote those figures in order to indicate that it was for the purpose of imposing false images. Let's start with the figure 3.225. You said that you came to that figure by subtracting the number of what is written as Sarajevo and specified municipality in table 2.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This number, 3.225, was arrived at using tables 1 and 3, which are identical, and you can see when the breakdown is made by municipalities within the city of Sarajevo, you see an indication that Sarajevo is undefined. If we have inside it persons both killed and wounded in an undefined Sarajevo, I believe they don't belong there. And by inference, they cannot be included in the sum total, and that's how the sum total was increased. That's --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are referring to the figure 573 in the part of table 1 that is subtitled "Opstina of event."

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, madam, the report of Tabeau et al. explicitly indicates that where place of event was unknown, it was excluded, whether it was possible or not that it could have been within Sarajevo. And at page 28 of the English version of the report - and that is section 5.1 - of the report of Tabeau et al. in a paragraph beginning "Regarding the statistics for opstina unspecified --" you explained. "Regarding the places of events, respondents usually reported names of local communities within the survey area or common names of particular locations within Sarajevo. We also saw names of municipalities different than the Sarajevo six or even countries other than Bosnia and Herzegovina. Some places were non-specific, such as airport, Pista, apartment, hospital, Kasina [phoen], Marsal Tito, et cetera. We developed a system of quotes for the reported place names in which every place was recorded into a local community. In place --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will you slow down, please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "If a place was located outside the front lines, the code of a municipality in Bosnia or country code was assigned. If a place could not be identified in terms of a local community but we knew that it was located within the front lines, one of the non-specific codes was used, opstina within front lines or opstina other or opstina unspecified." Madam, that explanation in the report, if, for example, one is to apply it, are there places, streets for example, that might be certainly within the front lines of Sarajevo in its entirety but overlapping more than one municipality, like Marsal Tito Street or downtown Sarajevo might encompass both Stari Grad and Centar, but isn't it possible that one could be certain that those places were within the front lines?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I find it hard to believe, because it reads on as follows: "A team of our Bosnian colleagues coming from Sarajevo or its surroundings assigned particular places to local communes. We also used maps of local communes, issued by the local authorities in Sarajevo. In this way, we were able to propose a classification of places that were available at the level of local communes. The federal -- the state institute for statistics in Sarajevo provided us with a bridging system for linking local communes with municipalities. Thus it became possible to group events by municipalities."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a different matter and we can now argue or not argue --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that assistance existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd -- if you'd please let the witness finish the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we'll have a break. Yes, please finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my personal view that what the Prosecutor just suggested is highly unlikely, and this term "undefined Sarajevo" does not mean this. If it were to mean what is suggested, there should be a footnote saying that Sarajevo could not be defined because certain places, certain parts or streets were not easy to identify. But this refers to areas that we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until ten minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague had to leave for reasons of health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hope it's not serious, Ms. Pilipovic. If you see him later, then you could pass to him our wishes that he feels better soon. Mr. Stamp, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in respect of the last question I asked, and that was in reference to the category opstina unspecified, which were counted within the figures for persons -- for casualties within Sarajevo, and I gave you two examples, situations where, for example, somebody might mention a street, which certainly is within downtown Sarajevo or within Sarajevo and that is within the confrontation lines but it may overlap one, two, or three municipalities or, for example, downtown Sarajevo, if that's the answer, which may also encompass more than one municipality within Sarajevo. And your answer was that you find it hard to believe and it's highly unlikely, and that is after I referred you to the explanation in the report of Tabeau et al. for that category. As an expert, if you are in doubt about something, wouldn't the right thing to do be to check the individual records and did you make an effort to check those individual records which were served on the Defence?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My only source was the report drawn up by Mrs. Tabeau. Checking up individual records was something that I had no opportunity to do. I had absolutely no insight into the raw material, so to speak. And my doubts are derived from the fact that I know the terrain, I know Sarajevo, and I know that there are no streets which cover more than one municipality. So I was unable to check is the answer to your question, but I firmly believe that this was impossible. And if I may add, from the report of Mrs. Tabeau, you simply cannot check that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, that is not an answer to my question. But let me check to see if I understand you correctly. Are you saying that there's no street in Sarajevo that was within the confrontation line, that ran -- or that overlapped more than one municipality? You know that to be a fact?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that. I believe that there are no such cases, although I can't guarantee that 100 per cent. Besides, I believe that the experts who were helping Mrs. Tabeau and whom she quotes here know this very well, and they can quote street names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition, street names in Sarajevo have changed a lot. At the moment when this is done, which is year 2001 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you again to listen to the question, to answer to the question, and if any further information is needed, you'll be asked for it. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I to understand that you would not concede or agree that, for example, the answer downtown Sarajevo may cover more than one local community?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. You mean the municipality centre?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, downtown Sarajevo may cover both Centar and Stari Grad; wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you define "centre." There is Centar as a municipality and there is centre, as downtown. We call Centar the area where, for instance, the theatre is located. What is your definition of Centar? Do you mean the Centar of the city or ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask it this way: If someone has asked about an event and the person responded that the event occurred in downtown Sarajevo, what local community -- or municipality would that be within Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. But if I heard something like that, I would think of Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is possible that it could be in more than one municipality -- may I rephrase that. It could be in one or another municipality.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't understand the question. It's possible that it's -- that the event takes place in several municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware -- or are you aware that in the statistics or the statistic techniques to be used in complex humanitarian emergencies you have to, in the matching process and in the rigorous processing of the data, you have to check the reports individually?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. If reports are available to you, then you have to check them. If they are not available to you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When -- at any time, before you wrote your report, while you were writing it, after you wrote it, did you become aware that all of the data used by Tabeau et al. had been given to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All I got was Mrs. Tabeau's report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask for the data, since you're aware that one should check the data individually for complex humanitarian emergency demographic investigations?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Did I ask the Defence team to give me access to the raw material --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- so that I can check all the data?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you ask. Check, for example, the Sarajevo unspecified that you say you're uncertain about or you don't believe but you can't be sure. Did you ask for the data so you could check it?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never tried to check the data. I believed the Tabeau report. I only disagreed with the way it was done. I didn't think that Mrs. Tabeau and her associates went about it the right way. They used sources which were not good, which were not defined, not complete --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- biased. And I didn't think it was my task to check whether Mrs. Tabeau defined a local commune properly or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't think it was your task to check whether Mrs. Tabeau defined a local commune properly or not? Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw from this Tabeau report --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say that, madam? Just simply, I want to understand what you just said. Did you just say that you didn't think it was your task to check whether Mrs. Tabeau defined a local commune properly or not? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that, but you didn't mention the local commune. You mentioned the background material. As far as local communes are concerned, I saw from the report that this was not verified and this was not good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your report at page 10 you also -- you gave the figure for a variety of characteristics of the sample and you say that these figures conflict. Again, this is the end of the second paragraph of section 2.1.1 of your report, and this is at page 10 of the English report.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the end where the table is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Section 2.1.1 of your report, the end of the second paragraph of that report, where you say, "Furthermore, a confusion of terminology, territory, and time is being used for purpose of imposing false images of the events which are being explained in the report. Thus as data from the same source and for the same space, that is, PDS 1994, several different magnitudes are given. For example, persons killed inside the front line in Sarajevo can amount to 3798, 3225, 3689, tables 1 and 6, but also 7879 and 6055 of table 2 or 2963, table 18." The number 3689, where did you find it in the report of Tabeau et al.?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Table 6. Table 6 shows persons killed within the front lines in Sarajevo, 9 September 1992 to the 10th of August, 1994. The total sum for this table is incorrect. For this first sum, broken down by manner of death, such as firearms, shelling, ending with firearms unspecified, this sum is 3.689. If you add to this those who directly fell victim in the war, 189, plus 229 for another value, plus accidental deaths, 82, plus unspecified and unknown, 184, you get a sum total of 3.600 -- a sum total of 4.099.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this number indicates the number of deaths by firearms broken down by the type of weapon. I indicated this because I thought this includes certain things that don't belong here, such as accidental deaths, and other casualties or unspecified --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without going into the mathematics, let me ask you: You're counting the figures in italics as well?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What italics? I don't have any italics in my text, so I don't know what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, well, the figures --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps first have a look at the B/C/S version of the -- so that it could -- it might be possible to easily clarify the issue. Could you provide us with the -- or no, I think I have the -- I haven't got the B/C/S version. Would you be willing to give us the translation that you used? Have you got it there? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I have a look?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I can tell you, I checked whether any italics appear in the table, and they do appear. I didn't check every item but -- as they appear in the original.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Then it means that I don't know what italics are. This here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Italics are -- I don't know how to translate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Cursive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that is not an upright position but just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I didn't understand the with word that was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the question remains whether you added all of the numbers or whether you excluded those in italics.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I added up all the figures. I didn't exclude any of those which are in italics. But if I may, there should be a footnote that something that is in italics has not been included in the sum total, and that is why I didn't think that one was supposed to subtract anything from it. The table needs to be clear so that everybody can know what it is about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You added everything. If -- and this is a suggestion -- if you just added the solid numbers given, then there would be no discrepancy. The italics, madam, refer to a breakdown of certain causes. If you add them, you will see that they sum up to the figure above, which is not in italics. Very well. You also said that -- well ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then if I may say so, such a table without an instruction how to use it - because the statistics prescribes very accurately how you have to do it - and if that was not done, then this is a kind of manipulation because there must have been a note as to what the sum total represents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you could not look at the table and figure this out for yourself.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Yes, I could have, but I didn't understand it. If one leaves aside the italics, because nowhere in the text or the table does it say what it means. There are certain rules to this particular profession and they must be obeyed, and it says "indicate what belongs where."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, you -- as you gave the figure 7879 as one of the variant numbers, can you see from table 2 and the explanations -- or isn't it clear to you from looking at table 2 of the Tabeau et al. report that 7879 refer to all the killings that came up or that were a result of all of the survey in all areas and at all dates? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This table again was not made according to the standards applied to statistical tables. It looks very dilettantish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, I'm not asking you for your opinions, about whether it is dilettantish or not, and what are the standards, I'm asking you simply, can you see that the reference to 7879 refers to the total number of events in the survey of persons killed in all areas, at all dates, including unknown areas and unknown dates? Are you aware of that; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot see it here because all is not defined. If we had all defined and we had the definition of what it is supposed to mean, then I would have known that. In this way, as it is presented here, I can only make guesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if you made a guess, madam, shouldn't you have indicated in your report that you are guessing that these numbers conflict instead of saying that the differences that you see indicate a dishonest motive, which is what you have said in your report? If you don't know something and you can only guess, why in your report do you put it down to a dishonest motive?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't put it that way, sir. I said that this was manipulation and that something was being shown that should not make part of this report. This is called human losses during the siege of Sarajevo from September 1992 until the 10th of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a yes or no answer. Let's move on quickly. And it seems -- very simply: Did you ask and did you get an opportunity to view or review the evidence of Ewa Tabeau in this court?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was read to me in December or January. And to be quite honest, I don't remember, but I am quite willing to answer if you have any questions in that regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall that in her evidence she explained, further than what is in her report, the meanings of these figures? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the question. And if I am correct, Mrs. Tabeau says that includes those who were not in Sarajevo, who were killed wherever, and said that it was 4500 to 5.000 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I understand your answer. Are you saying that having read the report of Tabeau et al. and listened -- or reviewed her testimony, you understand that the various figures refer to different characteristics of the sample survey? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think to my mind a simple explanation was that Mrs. Tabeau was manipulating, because she mentioned samples which are simply inadequate in this particular case. I could see no reason why she did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, we have time constraints. So you don't understand that these figures refer to different characteristics of the sample. You don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do not refer to different characteristics of samples. They refer to the absolutely same period of time and the same census.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except that the first figures --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, but may the witness be allowed to finish the answer to avoid any further problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As long as the answers are to the questions, she's allowed to finish them. When she's answering beyond what is asked, then she may be interrupted, unless there's a specific reason that there's something very important to explain. Then you'll have an opportunity to do that. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the next figure you gave, 6055, refer to the total number of persons killed in the indictment area during the indictment period and also at unknown dates? So that's a separate characteristic of a sample. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It does not refer --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that, but it doesn't refer to what you are saying. The figure of 6.055 cases covers the period between the 1st of January, 1992 to the 9th of -- no, to the 30th of September, 1994. The case --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- applies to the third column --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, madam. I didn't refer to table 2. Having reviewed the evidence of Ewa Tabeau, did you become aware that at the request of the Court she provided a further breakdown and clarification of table 2, which was an addendum to her report? Did you become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was given an addendum speaking of possible duplicates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given an addendum -- madam, listen to the questions I'm asking. Were you given an addendum which treated and elaborated upon table 2 of her report?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean a separate annex other than what was read in the transcript, then no, I did not get that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So perhaps you do not understand -- and you also give the number 2963 as a conflicting number. Are you aware that in the report at table 47 this is distinctly designated as HSS-94 based total number of persons killed in the indictment and indictment area and linked to the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are talking about 2.963?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have that in table 18. I don't have table 47. And I believe you said table 47.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I said page 47. But it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you said table 47 but you meant to refer to table 18 on page 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, page 47, and table 18. I see them, and I referred to them. I know that these are associated recorders, regardless of what I think about that. Fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want to know is does it -- did you not understand that the number 2963 referred to the HSS-based total number of persons killed in the indictment period in the indictment area which was linked to the 1991 census?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood that that figure was linked with 1991 census, but it does not apply to all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You knew that this figure was linked to the 1991 census and yet you say that it is an attempt to impose a false image and you do so by comparing it to the figure 3798, which is the only number in the entire report that she has given for the HSS-based total number of persons killed in the indictment period and indictment area in table 1. Knowing that she was referring to a separate characteristic of a sample, linked records, is it proper to make an allegation of that nature?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, because it is well nigh impossible to link up the records of the 1991 census and the 1994 census. And I will show it to you, if you allow me. If we take two different --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not the question. You use two figures and you compare them and say that she gives different figures for the same thing and therefore she is being dishonest, yet you now agree with me that you knew that she was not using the figure 2963 for the figure 3798, which is a total number of persons killed in the indictment period and indictment area. Is that a proper way to proceed?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that the data from the same source and for the same area give different figures, and I then use figures to show the differences without going into why they're different at this particular moment. So regardless of whether one is talking about a total or linked or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... You said also in your report - and this is at page 11 of the English text in the paragraph -- the third paragraph of section 2.1 -- sorry, section 2.1.1 - "It concluded that the total number of events in the PDS 1994 amounts to 37.057."

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it in the Serbian version. Can you please help me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is written that "It is concluded that the total number of events in the PDS 1994 amounts to 37.057 but that from this total number 20.151 events were in the area and in the period covered by this report. Without venturing here into the quality of the data, the question is raised as to how it is possible in the same area and in the same period that the same result is not established." Madam, the question is: At the time of writing your report, were you not aware that the two figures referred to two distinct sample characteristics, that is, 37.057 referred to all the records of events, that is, killings and woundings, natural deaths, whereas 20.151 referred to those records which were within the indictment period and indictment area? Simply put, weren't you aware that these two figures referred to two different characteristics of the sample?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are not different characteristics of the sample. The sample is the same and its characteristics are the same. It is said that the sum figure includes both what it should and what it shouldn't, and the second figure covers the period relevant for the indictment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Don't you understand and did you understand when you wrote your report that one figure referred to a whole, the complete total, and another figure is referring to something which is a part, a breakdown, of that total? Did you understand that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have to understand that because what you are saying is not true. These are two different periods. So one figure refers to the total, overall census of the 1st of January, and the second, what is supposed to be covered here, that is, from the 10th -- I've forgotten. I'll tell you. It's from the 10th of September, 1992 to the 10th of August, 1994. Then your expert says - and I'm quoting - "All phenomena which happened outside the period of siege or the area under siege and phenomena relevant for the siege were excluded from the sample referring to Galic." So this figure which we have here, 20.151, has to do with the Galic case. Figure 32.703 covers the whole census as of the 1st of January. I don't know why it is shown. But we are not dealing with two completely different samples. We have one in the same sample from which a part has been taken out, but not only this part is being shown but all the other parts which strictly speaking do not belong here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To move on to something else, so I could move quickly, I'm just going to suggest to you that the conflicts in figures that you referred to at page 31 of your report, in your table 1 - and that is at section 3.1 of your report - all reflect the fact that you have failed to understand that in the demographics in respect to complex humanitarian emergencies you need to record the various different sample characteristics and that these are not conflicting figures, they are figures for different phenomena, except, I should add, the figure you gave of 4081, which is again an example of double-counting or counting the numbers in italics.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This only shows -- this is only proof of how statistical data is manipulated. And in demography, at least in serious demography, that is not done. If you have a source of data which is called the expert opinion and which does not obey all the rules which are of importance for the profession and explanation what italics mean and what they do not, then it is manipulation. Besides, further proof of manipulation is that several samples are shown not as -- not compared, because we do not find comparative data here, not a single one. There are several samples, and they cover both those which refers to the Galic case and things that do not refer to the Galic case. I could have understood it had any comparison been made, some parts. But no, here we have only figures quoted which are in the comparative sense or of any other sense are of no relevance at all to the Galic case and then I see it as manipulation because one has to find one's way through without explanation, one has to accept those figures, and these are not through different samples. I repeat it. They are three say, identical samples of different sizes. One has 20.000, another with 37, and the third one 39. So they are not different sample. It is the same sample but different sizes of the sample, the same source of information, and the same period for the overall census from which we then derive the sample that should be applicable to the Galic case. So we do not have here three different samples and there's no comparison anywhere to be found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, it is clear from what you've just said that you do not understand the reason for identifying various sample characteristics, different characteristics of a same sample in the demographics used in complex humanitarian emergencies. So I'll ask you: Can you explain to us why in this particular situation would it be important to link the figures to the 1991 census? And I ask you that in respect, A, to the capture-recapture methodology and, B, in respect to determining a rate of events. Why in a demographic analysis is it important to link the survey records to the census?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is done so as to identify the population, that is, to confirm that that is the population from a particular area. That is all what this is about. And then possibly if there is a particular data missing, if you identify the person from the census so that you can check a particular information. It is not a matter how you do that. But the matching is a well-known practice. I do not think that anything here was properly identified. And if you are willing to listen to me, then I'll explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we should further listen to you tomorrow, because it's 7.00 and we have to finish. Unfortunately, we are not able to finish. Could you be available tomorrow in the afternoon? And we will certainly finish tomorrow. I'll tell you, we will. Dr. Radovanovic, would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for being available tomorrow. Mr. Stamp, I take it that it was a suitable time, because it's three minutes past 7.00, to break. Ms. Radovanovic, I instruct you again not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given in this court and you're still about to give in this court. And we'd like to see you back tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the same courtroom. Meanwhile, I would like to inform the parties that we expect to have a Status Conference or at least a hearing next Wednesday on the rebuttal evidence suggested by the Prosecution. So especially for the Defence, to have an opportunity to clarify its position in respect of the propositions made by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I understood that you said next Wednesday. I think the interpretation was wrong. But if we're talking about Wednesday, I'd like to know at what time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It will certainly be in the afternoon, but it also depends -- but may I first ask you, Mr. Usher, to escort Mrs. Radovanovic out of the courtroom because she might not be that interested in our procedural issues. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A precise time is not available, but I suggest that we'll have it -- need it to be confirmed that we start either at the usual time, at quarter past 2.00, or at 3.00. But perhaps we better start at quarter past 2.00. But the final time will be confirmed tomorrow. And meanwhile, if necessary, you could always ask Madam Registrar, because she will be aware of it by tomorrow morning. Yes. Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, quarter past 2.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: at 7.07 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 18th day of March, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
